scenario: [LEXP.3.7.3]: `x.bits(lo, w)` is int(floor(p / 2^lo) mod 2^w), p the 64-bit pattern of `x`. Rule `extracted` fires where `t.x.bits(t.lo, t.w)` equals the fact's `want`; every operand is an `Int` slot, so nothing folds. `abcd`: 0xABCD (43981) from bit 4, 8 bits wide, is 0xBC (188). `top`: -1 from bit 60, 4 bits wide, is 15: the field is the pattern's top nibble, all 1s, and it reads non-negative. `whole`: -1 from bit 0, 64 bits wide, is -1, `x.bits(0, 64)` being `x`. A builtin that shifted the signed value arithmetically would give `top` as -1, and one that masked a 64-bit width with `(1 << 64) - 1` would give `whole` as 0. PATH PINNED: FN_BITS in libds (`builtins.c`, `int_ops.h` `ds_i64_bits`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`).
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Int mutable
    lo: Int mutable
    w: Int mutable
    want: Int mutable

rule extracted:
    T t where t.x.bits(t.lo, t.w) == t.want
->
    log info "extracted {t.id}"
